status: development freeze before new raw gain experiments; cohorts previously inspected, not preregistration
objective: Test an explicitly limited engineering advantage of original uHNDI over absolute Target T; do not claim exclusive necessity or clinical superiority
primary_domain: Mendeley six-channel overnight EEG, unknown positive record-specific voltage gain applied equally to all channels and frequencies
power_gain_rule: voltage gain k implies power gain k squared, not k
threshold_rule: closest training ROC point to (0,1), train at nominal gain; no test retuning or sign selection
heterogeneous_gain_distribution: independent log-uniform k in [0.5,2] for each retained test recording, shared draws across methods
analytic_certificates: exact interval certificates under fixed nominal QC only; no continuous-range certificate asserted for reapplied QC
raw_recompute_audit: independently recompute Welch from scaled waveform on one clean and one maximum-peak block per retained EDF at k=.5,1,2; verify against k squared PSD
source_validation: recompute 42 EDF hashes and identity deduplication, validate all 41 nominal theta/alpha aggregates against historical store
negative_controls: Binder Target is already ITPC-derived and invariant to ideal voltage gain
Wielek stage proportions are not voltages; do not multiply them as amplifier simulation
frequency-dependent gains break the common-gain assumption; no universal robustness claim
success_interpretation: a proved gain-invariance property missing from raw T, plus correctly scoped empirical operational comparison; no claim that uHNDI is the only solution, clinically necessary, novel, or statistically superior in independent patients
historical_policy: read-only historical features, results, manuscripts and source; isolated results/gain_necessity_v3 outputs
